purpose: Trametinib is used to treat certain types of cancer, most commonly melanoma (a serious type of skin cancer) that has spread or cannot be surgically removed. It is also used for some lung cancers and other tumors that have a specific gene change called a BRAF mutation. It is often used together with another medicine called dabrafenib for better results.
how_it_works: Cancer cells sometimes have faulty signals inside them that tell them to grow out of control. Trametinib works by blocking a specific protein called MEK that is part of that faulty signaling pathway. By blocking this signal, the drug helps slow down or stop cancer cells from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Rash or acne-like skin changes, diarrhea, feeling tired or weak, swelling in your legs or feet, nausea, high blood pressure, headache, dry or itchy skin, and mouth sores. Some people also notice changes in their vision or sensitivity to sunlight.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious heart problems, including a weakened heart muscle, so your doctor will monitor your heart regularly. It can also cause serious eye problems, bleeding, blood clots, serious skin reactions, and lung inflammation. It may harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period after stopping. Tell your doctor right away if you have fever, vision changes, chest pain, unusual bleeding, or shortness of breath.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 2 mg taken by mouth once a day. It should be taken on an empty stomach — at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal. Try to take it at the same time each day. If you miss a dose, skip it if your next dose is less than 12 hours away.
